analysis:
Examined both NativeWorkerRuntime revisions and the complete added GemmaCheck source, including its metadata and continuation. NativeWorkerRuntime.swift:37–45 adds Gemma tensor-parallel dispatch with mandatory data-plane credentials, equal shares, no speculation/assistant policy, and forwarding of qualification and SSD key. Bootstrap-consumption enforcement remains at :80; generation still requires both request states retired (:121). All reservation, batch, cancellation, memory-release, ping and shutdown branches delegate to the new owner. No concrete bypass is visible in this wrapper.
GemmaCheck.swift adds locally invoked synthetic-model, generation, comparison, lane and collective diagnostics. Run/lane options are bounded and deadlines installed; report files contain generated tokens/logits and prompt digests. Bench sealing explicitly uses unauthenticated keys and is separate from the production wrapper's credential path. Comparison builds artifact identity from configuration rather than weight bytes; this diagnostic evidence alone must not establish durable build qualification (A-017/T-054). No supplied consumer shows that it does.
Integration must inspect Gemma4TensorParallelResidentRuntime.load and its request/batch paths: qualification enforcement and authenticated peer binding (TB-011/T-053), collective sealing/fail-closed behavior (TB-007/A-001), account-scoped cache lookup, encrypted SSD naming/payloads and key-unavailable behavior (T-041), and actual cancellation retirement/thread safety before the new capability assertion at NativeWorkerRuntime.swift:245 (T-010/T-028). These implementations and callers are outside this source scope; forwarded controls are not proof of enforcement. Also verify diagnostic reports cannot be mistaken for serving authorization or approved artifact evidence. No supported security regression can be established from these units alone.
